probable_cause: A severe vibration of the helicopter that led to the crew's inability to maintain sufficient rotor rotation speed (Nr), leading to excessive main rotor blade flapping, subsequent main rotor blade contact with the tail boom, and the resultant in-flight breakup. title: Airbus A330 223 · Seattle, WA (2016)
summary: The No. 1 engine fire was caused by a fuel leak that originated from a high cycle fatigue crack on the fuel nozzle No. 1 fuel manifold supply line. Fuel nozzle No. 1 is located at the 12 o'clock position on the engine, so the fuel that leaked from the crack ran down the diffuser case and ignited on the engine case surface. The diffuser case reaches high enough temperatures during engine operation to auto-ignite Jet A fuel.
probable_cause: A No. 1 engine fire caused by a fuel manifold supply line high cycle fatigue crack which led to a fuel leak that subsequently ignited on hot engine case surfaces. The fatigue crack originated and progressed due to elevated fuel manifold assembly vibration levels. Engine vibration testing identified a combustor tone that excites a natural (resonant) frequency of the fuel manifolds at specific engine speeds on Pratt & Whitney PW4000-94 and -100 inch fan series engines that feature a TALON II combustor.

probable_cause: The failure of the high-pressure turbine (HPT) stage 2 disk, which severed the main engine fuel feed line and breached the right main wing fuel tank, releasing fuel that resulted in a fire on the right side of the airplane during the takeoff roll. summary: West Air Sweden Flight 294 departed Oslo at 23:11 hours for Tromsø carrying 4.5 tonnes of mail. title: Aerosucr Fliht666
summary: A Boeing 727 operated by Aerosucre took off from Puerto Carreño with a load exceeding maximum takeoff weight. The crew set flaps to 30 degrees but used an incorrect rotation speed 5 knots higher than necessary. The aircraft did not become airborne in the available runway and traveled 95 meters over grass, striking a perimeter fence and a shed before becoming airborne at low altitude. The right main landing gear was detached, hydraulic damage occurred, and engine 3 lost power. The aircraft entered a right-hand descending turn and impacted flat terrain bursting into flames.

The airport was not approved for Boeing 727-200 operations and the civil aviation authority had not enforced this regulation.
